questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination based on an interest in the local culture and society. It was not my first visit, yet I knew that Mexican culture attracted me since I had already visited the country once before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In all seriousness, it was one of the best experiences of my life. However, it is crucial to keep in mind that an exchange stay is what you make of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly, this was fairly easy and the information was accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UDLAP had arranged an 'International Buddies' program to help those arriving in the airport get safely to Puebla. This created a sense of comfort and was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
There are multiple options for students above the age of 24 like myself, who are not eligible for living on campus. I will also recommend students to live off campus since the rules at UDLAP can be very strict and are enforced thoroughly by the guards and janitors. Some have described living on campus as a "police state". For instance, you are not allowed to drink or have people sleeping over in your dorm. You will also not have much privacy if you live in the dorms. 

I would recommend people using Cholula Capital and discourage students from using Charro Housing, particularly Casa Azteka since the owner of that specific house is a crook. Cholula Capital offer many good and comparatively cheap trips. The owner of the company is more serious than that of Charro Housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The many housing companies offer relatively cheap housing. The houses of Charro Housing are not exactly as they appear on the website with many being in much poorer condition than what is stated. These organizations often offer trips also, many of which you can do cheaper yourself with a couple of friends. 
Living off campus provides more freedom and you have more contact with the local community which I think is a definite plus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The fact that student housing organizations exist to support the on campus housing is great.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very confusing. In addition, when you are to have your courses pre-approved you will need to contact the international office to find the course descriptions since these are not in the course catalogue. This prolonges the process unneccesarily and can be quite frustrating to deal with. The website for the course catalogue is simply also very poorly and rather confusingly designed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to use an online portal, yet finding your courses and registering for them is somewhat confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact the international office physically or by email and they will be very willing to help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It happened but did not have to be so confusing.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for course descriptions at UDLAP in good time before you apply for your KU pre-approval of courses. If you study at the Master's level, you will have to contact the international office when registering courses for the second trimester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quality of educators was very varied. Great flexibility. Not too much stress, yet frustrating at times that you are so dependent on your group (group work is very prevalent) because sometimes getting an answer to messages from group members can be a very extensive process.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most were very insightful and the level was fitting, not too hard nor easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more group work. Less formal teaching setting. Less individual assignments. Softer deadlines. Lesser burden of work which I thoroughly enjoyed. Some semesters at KU, especially at the bachelor's level has an absolutely absurd work burden (2. semester in particular).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Economics. International Strategic Management. 
International Business. Company Talent and Culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Business Economics was pretty difficult as far as the math goes but the teacher was awesome. 
If you wish to really improve your knowledge on business you should choose 'International Strategic Management' since the teacher of this course Francois Duhamel is extremely knowledgeable. 
The rest are fine. Company Talent and Culture has a Swedish teacher who is also really nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food at restaurants are much cheaper than in Denmark, yet supermarket prices are almost the same. European products such as deoderant, etc. are more expensive. I was scammed by my housing organization out of 10.000 pesos. Public transport is much cheaper than Uber. 
You will find that you spend more on trips, etc. so that your monthly expenses will probably be higher than what you are used to from home even though you might think that the contrary is true given that you are in Latin America. Nevertheless, travelling in Mexico is still significantly cheaper than in many other locations.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
European products are more expensive than at home. 
Public transport has a reasonable price. Museums are free with student ID.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the activities that I partook in were arranged by the housing organizations. I did not make use of the offers that the university has so I do not feel capable of esteeming them. UDLAP seems to offer boundless activities to students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The UDLAP_informa email will bombard you with activities that you can partake in. I participated in a 'represent your country' activity which was fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make as many friends as you can early on, this will help you later.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Puebla, Veracruz, Oaxaca, CDMX and wherever else you feel comfortable. Close to Puebla avoid Guerrero and Michoacan due to safety.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mexicans are extremely inviting, friendly and open to foreigners. Their hospitality can be amazing such as when me and my friends were invited to a children's birthday party in CDMX with a family we randomly met.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make friends in class, your Mexican classmates will be open to hang out with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of timeliness can be frustrating at times. Mexican time is much more relaxed than what we have in Denmark which is closer to German time. You cannot expect people to show at the time that you have indicated. There are wild dogs everywhere, which can also be annoying yet mostly they will not do anything to you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The loving of fun and the hospitality. Mexicans truly know how to enjoy life (this will be very refreshing for you as a Dane).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do it. 
2) It will be awesome!
3) Bring warm clothes for the winter-time, especially for when you have to sleep since Mexican houses do not have heating.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cholula and Puebla is truly a great place to live. San Andrés and the downtown of Puebla are amazing locations. You live in the center of the country, which gives you good opportunities to travel around. Make friends so that you have someone to explore with.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social part. My international friends, travelling around the country with them and also the Mexican friends I made. It was also very fun for me to date Mexican girls as this gave me the opportunity to practice my Spanish and get an insight into the customs and ways of living of the locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Figuring out which of the many sweet girls I wanted to make my girlfriend ;) 

It can be rough to be away from home if you get sick or something similiar that sucks happens to you.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is awesome, you should certainly go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
